# Layergram 2.0.5 — Identity and release reliability

Layergram 2.0.5 strengthens identity startup, message export, contact import,
and cross-platform release reliability.

The release now:

- waits for secure identity storage before deciding whether onboarding is
  needed and offers a recoverable Retry state when storage cannot be read;
- prevents an existing installation from exposing a misleading
  create-identity action while identity data is loading or temporarily
  unavailable;
- preserves queued storage work when the active identity context changes;
- keeps Copy and Share export paths independently actionable and visibly
  reports failures;
- hardens contact verification, message-carrier processing, lifecycle recovery,
  and the opt-in system-keyboard security boundary;
- excludes QA diagnostics from production Android builds and verifies the
  required release manifest declarations; and
- adds regression gates for locked native dependencies, multi-ABI Android
  packaging, release disclosures, and the defects fixed in this release.

For users updating from a version earlier than 2.0.0, Layergram 2 retains the
protocol-v3 hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768 post-quantum identity and handshake,
combined classical/post-quantum ratcheting, and the Normal and Maximum
forward-secrecy modes. V3 changes the public identity and fingerprint from v2;
contacts must exchange and verify their complete v3 identity again.

Android open-source APKs remain signed with Layergram's dedicated direct-APK
certificate. Verify every download against the SHA-256 values published with
the release and on the Layergram website.
